title: Notification Service at Scale
intro: Design an enterprise notification dispatch platform distributing billions of notifications across Mobile Push (FCM/APNs), SMS, and Email.
objectives: Implement multi-vendor failover routing and deduplication.
Enforce user opt-out preferences and frequency-capping rate limiters.
body:
### Architecture Overview
1. **API Ingress**: Validates sender authentication, inspects payload schema, and queries User Preferences DB (opt-out settings, quiet hours).
2. **Prioritization Queues**: Critical notifications (2FA OTPs, fraud alerts) bypass marketing queues via dedicated high-priority workers.
3. **Vendor Gateways**: Decoupled worker microservices interfacing with external third-party providers:
   - iOS: Apple Push Notification service (APNs)
   - Android: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM)
   - SMS: Twilio, MessageBird (with automated multi-vendor fallback)
   - Email: SendGrid, Amazon SES
4. **Rate Limiting & De-duplication**: Redis sliding window limits user frequency (e.g. max 3 marketing emails/day).
keyIdea: Third-party vendors fail frequently. Isolate providers behind asynchronous queues with automated secondary vendor failover.

concepts.title: Idempotent Dispatch
concepts.body: Hashing `(user_id, event_type, event_id)` in Redis ensures double-taps by users never trigger duplicate billing SMS messages.

concepts.title: Delivery Analytics Loop
concepts.body: Webhook listener receiving delivery receipts, bounce rates, and click tracking from vendors.

examples: Uber dispatching real-time driver arrival notifications.

quiz.prompt: How should a notification service protect users from being spammed by marketing campaigns?
options: Enforce rate limiting and frequency capping based on user preference tables in Redis
Rely on third-party vendors to filter duplicates
Batch all notifications once a week
quiz.explanation: Frequency capping tables in Redis intercept and drop or delay lower-priority marketing messages exceeding user limits.
